analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: a new changelog entry and one table row in docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (line 372, the maintenance sweep row). No source code is in the batch, so the described behavior is not verifiable here. The row describes SSDWholeRootMaintainer caching readable DBK3 header verdicts keyed by lstat identity (dev, inode, size, mtime, ctime). The pass runs after every write job and skips reparsing unchanged files. Directory checks run once per fanout via fanoutPassesReadChecks. Failed reads are never cached, and TTL, budget and ownership decisions are said to be unchanged.

Relevant threat: T-041 (SSD cache at-rest tier). The documented design appears to preserve its mitigations. TTL expiry and budget eviction still apply to all files, and the cache of header verdicts lives only in memory. A file replaced or modified would change its lstat identity, and files touched by a hit are reparsed. A same-UID attacker could in theory preserve identity with forged timestamps, but inode and ctime changes make that hard. A remembered ownership verdict is not a trust grant, because AES-GCM authentication and identity binding still apply at read time.

Remaining integration questions for the code-side review, which are outside the supplied evidence: (1) whether the implementation compares the full identity tuple including ctime and inode; (2) whether the unchanged-header memory is invalidated on epoch or key rotation, so KEK wipe or epoch changes still lead to files being treated as unowned or deleted; (3) whether foreign or corrupt files still reach the same deletion or retention path; (4) whether running the sweep after every write job can starve writers or the removal lock (availability), compare T-060 and T-016. These are unverified contracts, not findings. No finding is raised from docs alone.
